text: One reason the AI boom is being underestimated is the GPU/TPU shortage. This shortage is causing all kinds of limits on product rollouts and model training but these are not visible. Instead all we see is Nvidia spiking in price. Things will accelerate once supply meets demand.

text: @ESYudkowsky @davidxu90 That may be true for your definition of "want"; but for a reasonable definition we can use for this purpose, an objective function placing value on X is good enough to make the system "want" X, in the same sense that evolution made humans mostly "want" to not kill other humans.

text: What are the strongest arguments against the possibility of an outcome where strong AI is widely accessible but there is a “balance of power” between different AI systems (or humans empowered by AI) that enables the law to be enforced and otherwise maintains stability?

text: I expect we will see continual progress from here to AGI, without any period that feels like a "winter". There are just too many obvious things left to be done. And the underlying exponential growth in compute has a very long way to go.

text: @AnthonyLeeZhang If trials become a bottleneck then yeah you'd want to have some form of AI juries, maybe as a first round before escalating the hardest cases to humans. But I would guess that AI-enabled mediation / prediction of jury outcomes could prevent the need for vastly more trials.

author: adamdangelo
text: @AnthonyLeeZhang I don't think vagueness has to change as part of this. AI seems like it will be quite good at handling uncertainty and ambiguity.

author: adamdangelo
text: I also expect we will transition to this world via a gradual, iterative process, and I think that will lead to a much lower risk of bad outcomes than counting on sudden major changes at the point when we have superintelligent AI.

author: adamdangelo
text: Possibly the worst takeaway you could have from web3 being overhyped and then failing to deliver is that the optimism around AI means it will fail to deliver. If there was ever a case for first principles thinking or digging into details beating pattern matching this is it.

author: adamdangelo
text: I think we are permanently done with AI winters. Endless summer from here on.

author: adamdangelo
text: In my view, this dynamic, combined with the ability for AI to accelerate its own progress, makes the advent of AI less like the internet and more like the industrial revolution. It should get society onto a permanently higher GDP growth rate, as long as we manage it well.

author: adamdangelo
text: The lack of this constraint about humans being in the loop means that unlike the internet, as AI gets better and better, GDP will be able to grow more and more in a way that keeps accelerating rather than getting us the diminishing returns of Amdahl's law.

author: adamdangelo
text: People will hopefully still play a role designing the systems or supervising them at a high level, but they won't need to be in the loop at all for the vast majority of economic activity.

author: adamdangelo
text: With AI the dynamic is totally different. Creating most goods and providing most services will no longer require humans in the critical path at all.

author: adamdangelo
text: but if that part of the process was only half of what was being done then you get at most a 2x gain. Since humans were still necessary for some part of most processes meant we ultimately got small gains to GDP, with diminishing returns as these technologies continued improving.

author: adamdangelo
text: Amdahl's law says that optimizing one part of a system can only improve the system by the amount that part is responsible for. You may speed up part of a process by 1000x by moving it to software...

author: adamdangelo
text: Those previous technologies ultimately effectively reduced friction for people to communicate and collaborate. But for almost all applications, the impact of the technology was limited by the fact that a human had to be in the loop.

author: adamdangelo
text: Pattern matching AI as "the next platform shift" like the PC/internet/smartphone leads to significant underestimates of its potential.

author: adamdangelo
text: My bet is this starts to happen within 4 years, e.g. measured US GDP growth is 3% instead of 2% and the change is largely attributed to AI. I am ignoring all the critiques about GDP being an imperfect measure of the economy here. I think it will be good enough for this purpose.

author: adamdangelo
text: The pace of change right now is unbelievable. We are going to be living in a very different world a year from now.
